title: Quiz: The Markov Property and Transition Matrices

options: The probability of the next state depends on the full history of all previous states
The probability of the next state depends only on the current state, not on how the process arrived there
All states in the chain must be equally likely
The chain must eventually return to its starting state
questions.explanation: The Markov property says P(X_{n+1}=j | X_0,...,X_n) = P(X_{n+1}=j | X_n). The current state X_n is a sufficient statistic — the entire history before step n adds no additional predictive information.

questions.text: An absorbing state i satisfies P_{ii} = 1 (the process stays in state i with probability 1 once entered).
questions.explanation: An absorbing state is one from which there is no escape: P_{ii} = 1 and P_{ij} = 0 for all j ≠ i. The entire row consists of zeros except for the diagonal entry, which is 1. Death in a clinical model is a classic absorbing state.

questions.text: A Markov chain with states {Healthy, Mildly Ill, Severely Ill, Dead} where Dead is absorbing. Is this chain irreducible?
options: Yes — all four states can communicate
No — Dead cannot transition to Healthy, Mildly Ill, or Severely Ill
Yes — as long as the other three states communicate with each other
It depends on the specific values of the transition probabilities
questions.explanation: An irreducible chain requires every state to be accessible from every other state. Since Dead is absorbing (P_{D,D}=1), it cannot reach Healthy, Mildly Ill, or Severely Ill. Therefore Dead does not communicate with the other states, and the chain is NOT irreducible.

questions.text: Why is the Markov property described as a 'massive simplification' for modelling disease progression?
options: It means the disease always gets better over time
It eliminates the need for any data — the chain can be specified from theory alone
Instead of tracking the entire patient history to predict tomorrow's state, only today's state is needed
It guarantees that the chain has a stationary distribution
questions.explanation: Without the Markov property, the transition probability depends on the full history (X_0, X_1, ..., X_n), which requires exponentially more data and computation as time grows. The Markov property collapses this to a single current-state condition.

questions.text: In the 4-state model with TPM P, what does the entry P^{10}_{H, D} represent?
options: The probability that a Dead patient becomes Healthy in 10 steps
The probability that a Healthy patient is Dead after exactly 10 weeks
The average number of steps from Healthy to Dead
The fraction of the transition matrix attributable to death
questions.explanation: P^{(10)}_{H,D} = (P^{10})_{H,D} is the (H, D) entry of the 10-step transition matrix. It gives the probability of starting in state H (Healthy) and being in state D (Dead) after exactly 10 time steps — a 10-week mortality risk for a currently-healthy patient.

questions.text: If the Markov property holds, then knowing a patient was Severely Ill 3 weeks ago (but is currently Mildly Ill) gives additional information about where they will be next week.
questions.explanation: Under the Markov property, only the current state (Mildly Ill) is relevant for predicting next week's state. The fact that the patient was Severely Ill 3 weeks ago is already 'encoded' in their current state — the history provides no additional predictive power beyond the present state.
